english_classification.chapter_title: The Second, concerning the Parable of the Tree.
english_classification.chapter_note: This chapter is heavily overlaid with editorial material. The first half (¶1-11) is almost entirely dialogue frame, Gospel citation, and anti-sectarian polemic — the editors use Jesus' parable as a proof-text and argue against 'the sects' using NT examples (Judas, Paul, the date palm). The substrate teaching emerges in the second half with the five-fold faculty mapping: consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind → cosmic beings/locations for both the good tree (ascending: holy church → Pillar of Glory → First Man → Third Ambassador → the Father) and the bad tree (descending: law of death → transmigration → gehenna → vessel → the lump). This systematic faculty-realm correspondence is the oldest layer. The chapter closes with a dualistic creedal assertion (the two trees did not arise from one another) wrapped in exhortation. The editorial fatigue pattern is confirmed: substrate vocabulary increases in the second half while frame/institutional vocabulary drifts upward. The 'taste' mappings (good tree → holy church/catechumens; bad tree → the sects) are editorial applications that reach outside the cosmic system into contemporary institutions.
